detail.longDescription: I'm testing the new sentinel type in Python 3.15. I want to use a sentinel to distinguish a missing value from None . Here is my code: import json MISSING = sentinel("MISSING") data = { "name": "John", "age": MISSING } print(json.dumps(data)) This raises a TypeError because the sentinel is not JSON serializable. I also tried converting it to a string: data["age"] = str(MISSING) encoded = json.dumps(data) decoded = json.loads(encoded) print(decoded["age"] is MISSING) But this returns False . Is there a simple way to serialize a sentinel to JSON and restore it as the original sentinel object when decoding, while keeping it different from ordinary strings?
